question.leadin: Albert Einstein turned down the presidency of this country.
question.text: Identify this country that declared independence in 1948 following the end of British rule in Mandatory Palestine. It is the only officially Jewish country in the world.
question.clue: This country's early "Austerity" period led it to sign a reparations agreement with West Germany under its first leader David Ben-Gurion.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about royal titles.
swap.text: This Arabic title signifies that a ruler is the political leader of all Muslims. Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali are called "Rightly Guided" (these).
swap.clue: The assassination of a holder of this office sparked the First Fitna, during which his successor won the Battle of the Camel against Aisha.

question.leadin: Some Westernizing efforts in this country included educational reforms under the advisement of John Dewey and the Hat Law of 1925, which banned the use of the fez in favor of more Western-style hats.
question.text: Name this country which had its borders redefined in the Treaty of Lausanne. Soon after, this country moved its capital to Ankara, though its most populous city is Istanbul.
question.clue: After allegedly either smuggling or fabricating Yortan culture artifacts from this country in the Dorak Affair, James Mellaart was banned from leading the excavation of Catalhoyuk .

swap.leadin: Nuri al-Maliki tried to catch a shoe after it was thrown in protest of this war.
swap.text: Name this war protested by Muntadhar al-Zaidi, during which Saddam Hussein was executed in its namesake country.
swap.answerHtml: Iraq War [or Second Persian Gulf War; do not accept or prompt on “Persian Gulf War” alone]
swap.clue: A speech in front of a "Mission Accomplished" banner falsely celebrated the end of this war.

question.leadin: This man adopted the "Three Nos" policy after losing the Six Days War.
question.text: Name this man who nationalized the Suez Canal and constructed the Aswan High Dam.
question.clue: He greatly enhanced the power of the General Intelligence Directorate, and earlier, this man founded a secret organization with Abd al-Hakim Amir, Zakaria Mohieddine, and his own future successor.

swap.text: In 106 CE, the Roman emperor Trajan annexed the Nabatean kingdom in order to protect a road which had linked Alexandria to this city, a center of steel production. It was the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate.
swap.clue: The reputed discovery of Father Tomaso's bones led to the arrest of six members of this city's Jewish community in an 1840 affair that inspired Sultan Abdulmecid to issue an anti-blood libel firman.

question.text: This dynasty replaced the Fatimids in Egypt. It was led by its namesake's Kurdish son Saladin.
question.clue: This dynasty lost territory under al-Adil and al-Kamil, and was finally driven out of its chief territory following the Battle of al-Mansurah.

swap.leadin: This man was found with a gold-plated Browning Hi-Power pistol, referencing his son's Khamis Brigade, at the time of his capture.
swap.text: Name this leader from Sirte, who came to power by overthrowing his country's King Idris. In 2003, this leader accepted responsibility for the Lockerbie bombing.
swap.clue: This man was overthrown by the National Transitional Council after the Battle of Sirte ].

question.text: The Hurrian language is related to the Urartian ("oo-RAR-tee-an") language, spoken in a civilization that has become a part of the history of this country, which converted to Christianity under St. Gregory the Illuminator.
question.answerHtml: Armenia [or Republic of Armenia or Hayastani Hanrapetut’yun] (Gregory made Armenia the world’s first Christian country.)
question.clue: A ruler of this kingdom abandoned the worship of deities like Anahit in favor of Christianity to curb Sassanian influence and built the world's oldest cathedral in Etchmiadzin .

swap.leadin: This group established the consecutive Bahri and Burji dynasties, which began after Aybak established a sultanate shortly before his murder by Shajar al-Durr.
swap.text: Identify this military group that overthrew Turanshah and ended the Ayyubid dynasty after resisting Louis IX's crusade at the Battle of Fariskur.
swap.answerHtml: Mamluks [or Mamelukes; despite the claims of Wikipedia, do not accept “Marmaduke,” who is a fictional dog and not a Muslim soldier]
swap.clue: Barquq("bar-kuk")overthrew the last Kipchak ruler of these people and began their Circassian-dominated Burji ("bur-JEE") dynasty.

question.leadin: The Treaty of Hudaybiyah was signed between Mecca and this city.
question.text: Name this city, the second-holiest city in Islam.
question.clue: A violation of a pact with this city's leaders led to the execution of the Jewish tribe of Qurayza .

swap.leadin: This battle is commemorated by the holiday of Ashura, which is celebrated during the month of Muharram.
swap.text: Name this 680 AD battle in which a small force led by Muhammad's grandson Husayn was wiped out in Iraq. It triggered the Second Fitna, or Islamic civil war.
swap.clue: Prior to this battle, the governor of Al-Basrah was sent by Yazid I to warn tribal leaders of reprisal if they fail to keep order among their people.

question.leadin: Nadia Maria El Cheikh argues that gendered metaphors used to describe jahl in this empire degraded the status of women.
question.text: Name this empire which secured a copy of Ptolemy's Almagest for an institution that began as a library for either Al-Mansur or Al-Ma'mun.
question.clue: Several of its rulers relied on the Barmakids to administer it, and the Buyids later conquered its capital, built by al-Mansur.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about medieval Islamic caliphates.
swap.text: When this caliphate was ended by the Abbasids in 750 CE, one son of the royal family escaped to Iberia and continued the dynasty there.
swap.clue: Abu Muslim's revolt against Marwan II ended this dynasty at the Battle of the Zab River.

question.leadin: This man fought the Ridda Wars to combat apostasy, during which he was ably served by Khalid ibn al-Walid.
question.text: Name this man, who, after Mohammed's death, became the first Caliph, starting the Rashidun Caliphate and the process of Islamic expansion.
question.clue: Lubaina, Zinnira, and Bilal were among the many slaves this man used his wealth to emancipate , and the rest of his money went to fund an expedition at Tabuk.

swap.leadin: Chris Alexander, Canada's Citizenship and Immigration Minister, briefly suspended his reelection campaign after this boy's death.
swap.text: Name this boy whose family wished to enter Canada after fleeing as refugees from Syria. This three-year old boy's body was found washed up on a Turkish beach, prompting international outcry.

question.text: This group, composed of anti-government forces, would be the target of any chemical attack by the Syrian government. It has been in a state of rebellion for over a year.
question.answerHtml: Syrian National Coalition [or National Coalition for Syrian Revolutionary and Opposition Forces, or Coalition Nationale]

swap.text: Until the late 1960s, the Binladin Group had the exclusive contract to renovate this holy site, a mosque that shares its name with a militant wing of the Fatah Party.
swap.answerHtml: Al-<u>Aqsa</u> Mosque [or Al-Masjid al-<u>Aqsa</u>; accept Al-<u>Aqsa</u> Martyrs’ Brigade or Kata’ib Shuhada al-<u>Aqsa</u> or Masjid <u>Bayt al-Maqdis</u>; prompt on “<u>Farthest</u> Mosque” or “Mosque of the <u>Holy City</u>”]
swap.clue: This place, which members of the Gush Emunim had planned on blowing up during the 1980s. This place is also where a visiting King Abdullah I was assassinated in 1951.

question.text: Meanwhile, this agreement to divide the Middle East into British and French spheres of influence was undermining the promises made to Husayn.
question.clue: One party to this agreement issued the Bassett Letter to reassure an ally of their territorial aspirations after this agreement was made public in the newspapers Pravda and Izvestia; that ally was Hussein bin Ali.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the assassinations of some 20th Century Middle Eastern leaders, FTPE.
swap.text: The son of the Kataeb Party's founder, this man organized and commanded the Lebanese Forces to combat Syrian occupation. Elected as Lebanon's president in 1982, he was killed in a bomb blast before he could take office, and his brother Amine was elected as his replacement.
swap.clue: This leader of the Phalangist Party, who united the Maronite militias of Lebanon. His party emerged victorious from the 1982 Lebanon War with Israeli support and the expulsion of the PLO.
